question: A 32-year-old man is newly diagnosed HIV-positive. CD4 count is 350 cells/μL. He has no active opportunistic infections. According to NACO guidelines, what is the correct management?

answers.text: Defer ART until CD4 count falls below 200 cells/μL

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This is outdated practice. NACO adopted the 'Treat All' policy — ART is indicated for all PLHIV regardless of CD4 count or WHO stage.

answers.text: Start ART with TLD (tenofovir + lamivudine + dolutegravir) immediately

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Under NACO 'Treat All', ART should be initiated for all PLHIV at any CD4 count. The preferred first-line regimen in India is TLD (tenofovir disoproxil fumarate 300 mg + lamivudine 300 mg + dolutegravir 50 mg) — a single fixed-dose combination tablet once daily.

answers.text: Start ART with TLE (tenofovir + lamivudine + efavirenz) as TLD is reserved for treatment failure

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: TLE is the older first-line regimen. NACO guidelines updated the preferred first-line regimen to TLD due to its higher genetic barrier to resistance, fewer neuropsychiatric side effects, and once-daily fixed-dose convenience.

answers.text: Defer ART for 2 weeks to complete baseline investigations before initiating

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Baseline investigations (CD4, viral load, creatinine, HBsAg, RPR) should be done, but ART should be initiated promptly. Investigations should not cause undue delay in starting treatment.

overallFeedback.feedback: Key NACO policy: 'Treat All' means NO CD4 threshold for starting ART. The preferred regimen is TLD (tenofovir + lamivudine + dolutegravir) — memorise this as India's standard first-line.
Excellent. NACO 'Treat All' — TLD is the preferred first-line regimen for adults and adolescents with HIV in India. Single tablet once daily simplifies adherence.
